content.title: Five-year-old found dead after IAN Alert

Kentucky State Police issued an IAN Alert—for missing or endangered people. The boy was found dead hours later. (Kentucky State Police) NEWS 5-year-old dies after wandering away from home BY Deborah Harbsmeier Kentucky UPDATED 12:38 PM ET Jul. 15, 2025 PUBLISHED 12:20 PM ET Jul. 15, 2025 PUBLISHED 12:20 PM EDT Jul. 15, 2025 SHARE CUB RUN, Ky. — A 5-year-old boy is dead after he wandered away from his home in Cub Run, Kentucky. What You Need To Know Silas Chearer, 5, was reported missing from his Hart County home at 8 a.m. Kentucky State Police issued an Immediate Alert Notification The austic boy was wearing only his pajamas KSP issued another IAN Alert when the found the boy, who was dead Kentucky State Police issued an Immediate Alert Notification, which hit cellphones across the state. Silas Chearer walked away from his house wearing his pajamas at approximately 8 a.m. The little boy was autistic. A few hours later, another IAN Alert was sounded. KSP announced they had found Chearer. A KSP release said, “Tragically, he was found deceased. KSP grieves with this family and the community.” IAN Alerts became law in Kentucky in 2024. IAN Alerts and AMBER Alerts are both emergency alert systems, but have different criteria for activation. IAN Alerts are for missing children under 18 who have intellectual disabilities or mental illness and who may be in danger. AMBER Alerts are specifically for abducted children who are believed to be in immediate danger.
